your_book:
Friday was a tale of two sessions for Jaleel's book. The biggest single-day damage came from LULU (−17.4%, −21.3% unrealized), which hit an 8-year low ahead of its incoming CEO transition — a guidance cut from June is still bleeding into price with no sign of stabilization. ADBE (−6.7%, +8.7% unrealized) also took a meaningful hit, extending the post-beat selloff driven by AI-moat narrative fears and the CFO exit; earnings land September 10, so this one has a hard catalyst coming fast. EFX (−6.4%) dropped sharply with no company-specific headline, likely caught in broader risk-off flows. On the positive side, BSX (+1.8%) bounced despite carrying an elevated risk flag on its slashed guidance, and NVDA (+0.84%) edged up even as chip peers faced pressure from Fed rate-hike commentary — though export-control risk remains live.

The drift worth watching sits in LULU and RKLB. Both are in unrealized loss territory (−21.3% and −18.0%, respectively), and RKLB carries an AVOID verdict with a QARP of just 39 — the weakest quality score in the book by a wide margin. These two are where price and thesis have diverged most sharply. ONON (−10.9% unrealized, STRONG BUY) is quietly sliding too and deserves monitoring. Meanwhile, AZN slipped −1.3% today and sits just barely underwater at −1.1% overall — a name rated STRONG BUY that hasn't delivered yet.

Looking ahead, the ADBE earnings report on September 10 is the nearest hard catalyst. The pharma cluster — AZN, NVS, GILD, NBIX, VRTX — faced broad pressure today, weighed partly by drug-pricing policy overhang. ABT (−0.4% today but +25.3% overall) remains the steadiest large position; its trimmed EPS guide is a yellow flag, not a crisis, with the next update October 13.

attention.headline: Down 17% today, −21% unrealized — thesis is broken on the numbers
attention.note: Five straight quarters of negative Americas comps, margin destruction from tariffs, China stalled, and now an 8-year price low days before a CEO change; the BUY verdict needs to be stress-tested against the actual guidance trajectory, not the hoped-for recovery.

attention.headline: Earnings September 10 — narrative, not fundamentals, is driving the selloff
attention.note: A −6.7% session drop with a live catalyst in six days means the position needs a pre-earnings decision framework now: hold through the print or reduce to limit binary risk given the CFO exit and AI-disruption overhang.
